channel.title: The Bureau of Investigative Journalism - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Bureau of Investigative Journalism (thebureauinvestigates.com)

item.title: After a string of failures, what next for the ‘crackdown’ on SLAPPs?
item.description: Analysis: Until lawyers are barred from sending out empty threats on behalf of mega-rich clients, free speech remains in danger

item.title: Privacy for your ‘guests’: Mandelson’s email to Epstein recommending exclusive villa
item.description: Redacted email deciphered by TBIJ shows former politician suggesting holiday home for convicted sex offender

item.title: Epstein details scrubbed from Mandelson’s Wikipedia page by shady paid editor
item.description: As the then-ambassador came under fire, an anonymous user tried to downplay his history of support for Jeffrey Epstein

item.title: Cancer drugs are being scrapped at huge scale after quality failures in Peru
item.description: Tens of thousands of vials have been pulled from shelves at the last minute because the country keeps buying dangerous drugs

item.title: As men dominate the Epstein Files headlines, we must listen to the voices of the survivors
item.description: The files’ shocking details read like an extreme expression of the sexism that many of us are familiar with

item.title: Mother vindicated after top judge overturns evidence of parental alienation expert
item.description: Findings based on the evidence of Melanie Gill are thrown out by high court – and could open the door for more of the families affected

item.title: Government slammed for ‘callous’ inaction on farmworkers abuse
item.description: Criticism comes after the rejection of various ideas, put forward by its own advisers, on how to protect migrant workers from exploitation

item.title: MPs pledge to investigate toxic gas from animal farming
item.description: Government inquiry into air pollution will zero in on ammonia after we revealed a surge in levels around chicken farms

item.title: The world after Epstein: a watershed moment in the fight against corruption?
item.description: Bad apples, black sheep, lone crooks – the old excuses no longer hold water. And politicians will have to act accordingly

item.title: Triumph for transparency as court reporter wins battle for private documents
item.description: Judge grants access to psychological reports in ruling that could open door for court reporters seeking public-interest documents
